summary: The first mismatch is a JavaScript preflight refusal on an awake killer bee. C monmove.c:dochug applies bee_eat_jelly only when royal jelly is under the bee and the helper consumes its turn, then continues to the ordinary attack path otherwise; the JavaScript guard rejects the bee before that source condition. The case reaches poisoned() later at step 36, after the step-34 refusal.

source.branch: For an awake killer bee in dochug(), C first processes PHASE TWO, then in PHASE THREE checks whether LUMP_OF_ROYAL_JELLY is on the bee square and calls bee_eat_jelly() only then. C returns from the turn only if the helper returns >= 0; it proceeds through ordinary movement and PHASE FOUR attacks when the item check fails or bee_eat_jelly() returns -1 (a queen is already present). The recorded C attack at step 34 proves that no consuming/transformation result ended that turn, but does not distinguish absent jelly from the existing-queen return. The JavaScript assertSimpleActionState() instead rejects every awake killer bee before this source decision. Fix that general preflight boundary so it follows the supported dochug path and preserves the special-action result when it actually consumes a turn.
callers: allmain.c:moveloop_core:212 calls mon.c:movemon:1320, which enters monmove.c:dochugw:214 and then monmove.c:dochug.
monmove.c:dochug:971 calls mhitu.c:mattacku from PHASE FOUR when the hostile bee is in range, not scared, and the hero is alive; hitmu records the landed sting.

JavaScript planning path: allmain.js:planElapsedTurn invokes unported_monster_actions.js:runSimpleMonsterAction; runSimpleMonsterAction calls assertSimpleActionState at :1484 before monmove.js:dochugw reaches its source-backed killer-bee check.
dependencies: invent.c:sobj_at supplies the PHASE THREE floor-object predicate for LUMP_OF_ROYAL_JELLY; js/monmove.js:2684-2687 already uses it before bee_eat_jelly().
monmove.c:bee_eat_jelly and find_pmmonst decide whether the bee consumes its move, dies, or returns -1 because a queen already exists; js/monmove.js contains both helpers and their caller.
monmove.c:distfleeck precedes the special-action check, and mhitu.c:mattacku/hitmu own the ordinary attack reached by this recording.
